## TL;DR

Resumed task #1061 from a failed review pass. Corrected stale check-gate recovery to inspect the lock's holder list, adjusted two regression tests to model the queued file snapshot and dead-holder schema accurately, formatted the branch, and reran the scoped RepoOS gate. The focused check-gate suite passed, followed by a green `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check`.

## Work and rationale

The previous full gate had failed TypeScript because recovery referenced `lock.pid`, a field removed when locks moved to the multi-holder format. I changed recovery to determine liveness from `lock.holders`, the same representation used by acquisition and release. This preserves a lock whenever any holder is still alive and allows reconciliation to clear it when all holders are dead.

The failed run also exposed two outdated test assumptions. The queue snapshot test enqueued the current task-file contents and only modified the file afterward, which no longer represented the queued commit's intended state. I moved the test edit before enqueue so it verifies that the captured snapshot is what flush commits. The crash recovery test changed a legacy top-level PID, but current locks encode PID per holder; it now marks each holder PID as dead. These updates exercise the current persisted format and snapshot behavior directly.

I first reran `tests/check-gate-bookkeeping.test.ts`; all 14 tests passed. The first complete scoped check then passed its remote build, tests, UI smoke and contrast stages, but failed the local formatter check. I ran `bun run fmt` and repeated the complete gate. Remote validation initially hung on `thinkpad`; RepoOS detected the hang and retried on `bee`. That validation passed all 467 scoped test files (6,629 passing tests and one skipped), and local validation passed the formatter, lint, build, UI smoke, contrast, task asset, bare-require and user-docs build checks.

## Approaches tried

- Ran the focused gate-lock test file first to isolate the two failures from the larger suite; this confirmed both corrections.
- Ran the required full scoped check. The first pass identified formatting drift, so I formatted the branch and reran the complete check instead of treating the remote green result alone as sufficient.
- Allowed RepoOS's managed remote validation to retry after its first host reported a hung container. The retry completed successfully.

## Challenges and blockers

The remote runner repeatedly became silent during initial attempts, adding substantial wall time. RepoOS's automatic hung-container detection and host retry resolved this without changing the validation procedure. The final scoped check completed successfully. No manual status change or hand-commit was made; RepoOS created its normal WIP checkpoint for validation.

## Key learnings

Persisted lock recovery must evaluate every holder rather than a removed single-process field; otherwise a recovered process can either leave a stale lock or ignore a live one. Queue tests must place the intended file state before enqueue, because snapshots deliberately preserve state per queued commit. Tests that simulate crashes must use the current on-disk schema, including holder-level PIDs. Finally, a passing remote suite does not replace local format and repository guard checks: the first full pass caught formatter drift, and the post-format rerun verified the final checked tree.
